newsitem.title: INDIA: Dengue fever kills 19 in Indian capital.
newsitem.headline: Dengue fever kills 19 in Indian capital.

text.p: An unusually dangerous strain of tropical dengue fever has killed 19 people in the Indian capital since the middle of last month, a doctor said on Wednesday.

Dr D.C. Jain, of the National Institute of Communicable Diseases, told Reuters that 267 cases of the mosquito-borne disease had been reported since August 18. At least seven victims had died since Monday, he said.
Dengue, also called breakbone fever, is normally accompanied by high fever, muscular and joint pain and headaches. It runs its course in six to seven days.
The disease is especially prevalent during the monsoon rains, when mosquitoes breed in stagnant water.
Jain said a dangerous strain that causes internal bleeding had appeared but that the number of fresh dengue cases had dropped, easing concerns.
